blocks.prompt: 9. [printed as 8.] Find the area of the region bounded by the curve \(y = (x - 1)(x + 1)(x - 2)\) and the \(x\)-axis.
blocks.explanation:
Yeh cubic hai jis ke teen roots hain, is liye yeh \(x\)-axis ke saath do regions band karti hai: ek upar aur ek neeche.
Total area dono ke sizes ka jama hai (3.7.1 ka Note 3).
Agar hum seedha \(-1\) se \(2\) tak ek integral le lein to neeche wala hissa minus ho kar jawab chhota kar dega, is liye torna zaroori hai.
Plan: roots, har tukre par sign, expand, har tukre ka integral, phir absolute values jama.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(y = (x - 1)(x + 1)(x - 2)\) aur \(x\)-axis.
Maloom karna: kul band area.
Tareeqa: Total area \(= \int_{-1}^{1}|y|\,dx + \int_1^2 |y|\,dx\), yani har region ka size alag nikal kar jama.

Qadam 1: Roots aur signs
Roots: \(x = -1, 1, 2\).
\(x = 0\) par: \(y = (-1)(1)(-2) = 2 > 0\) (\([-1, 1]\) par upar).
\(x = 1.5\) par: \(y = (0.5)(2.5)(-0.5) = -0.625 < 0\) (\([1, 2]\) par neeche).
Kyun: Band regions lagatar roots ke darmiyan hote hain. Har tukre mein ek test point se sign pata chal jata hai.
Dhyan dein: Roots ko chhote se bare tarteeb mein likhiye: \(-1, 1, 2\); warna limits ghalat lag jati hain.

Qadam 2: Expand karein
\[(x^{2} - 1)(x - 2) = x^{3} - 2x^{2} - x + 2\]
\[F(x) = \dfrac{x^{4}}{4} - \dfrac{2x^{3}}{3} - \dfrac{x^{2}}{2} + 2x\]
Kyun: Pehle \((x - 1)(x + 1) = x^{2} - 1\) (difference of squares), phir \((x - 2)\) se multiply. Polynomial ko power rule se term by term integrate karna aasaan hai.

Qadam 3: \(F\) ki values
\[F(-1) = \dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{2}{3} - \dfrac{1}{2} - 2 = -\dfrac{19}{12}\]
\[F(1) = \dfrac{1}{4} - \dfrac{2}{3} - \dfrac{1}{2} + 2 = \dfrac{13}{12}\]
\[F(2) = 4 - \dfrac{16}{3} - 2 + 4 = \dfrac{2}{3}\]
Kyun: Common denominator 12 rakha: \(F(-1) = \frac{3 + 8 - 6 - 24}{12}\), \(F(1) = \frac{3 - 8 - 6 + 24}{12}\).
Dhyan dein: \(x = -1\) par \(-\frac{2x^{3}}{3} = -\frac{2(-1)}{3} = +\frac{2}{3}\); cube ka minus sign sambhal kar.

Qadam 4: Dono tukre
\[\int_{-1}^{1} y\,dx = \dfrac{13}{12} + \dfrac{19}{12} = \dfrac{32}{12} = \dfrac{8}{3}\]
\[\int_{1}^{2} y\,dx = \dfrac{8}{12} - \dfrac{13}{12} = -\dfrac{5}{12}\]
Kyun: Doosra tukra negative aaya kyunke wahan curve neeche hai, jaisa Qadam 1 ne bataya tha.

Qadam 5: Total area
\[A = \dfrac{8}{3} + \dfrac{5}{12} = \dfrac{32 + 5}{12} = \dfrac{37}{12}\]
Kyun: Dono regions ke sizes jama kiye; \(-\frac{5}{12}\) ka size \(\frac{5}{12}\) hai. Jama karne ke liye \(\frac{8}{3}\) ko \(\frac{32}{12}\) likha taake denominator ek ho jaye.

Tasdeeq:
Poora signed integral \(\int_{-1}^{2} y\,dx = F(2) - F(-1) = \frac{8}{12} + \frac{19}{12} = \frac{27}{12}\), aur tukron se bhi \(\frac{32}{12} - \frac{5}{12} = \frac{27}{12}\). Dono mil gaye, is liye hisaab sahi hai.
